text:
sam: Nightly perf dashboard fired an alert — kernel routing entropy jumped, 95p latency +120ms vs baseline around 02:15 UTC. tagging @eng-runtime :alarm:

elaine: saw it. looks correlated with last merge to release/x. commit: https://git.internal/r/redwood/merge/0x9f3a2

liam: starting an automated bisect on release/x now. initial smoke on CI showed throughput -18% on small-seq workloads.

ci-bot: [perf-ci] job perf/smoke-small-seq failed on commit 0x9f3a2 — delta: p95 +118ms, tokens/s -17%. link: https://ci.internal/build/71234 :warning:

mira: can someone grab a quick profile? want to know if it's kernel selection or batching heuristic change.

liam: profile attached (summarized):
```
hotspots:
  runtime::kernel_selector::score  42%
  runtime::batcher::dispatch       18%
  kvcache::lookup                 12%
  decode::attention_kernels       10%

kv cache miss rate: 0.41 (was ~0.04 baseline)
mean batch size: 2.1 (was 3.6 baseline)
```

elaine: that KV miss rate jump is huge. commit 0x9f3a2 changed kernel scoring to favor entropy-based kernel for short sequences + removed a small-width quantized path selector. probably falling back to heavier kernel and thrashing KV entries.

tom: repro locally with the nightly sample set: `./run_perf.sh --seq-dist short --kernel-scan` shows the same p95 bump. quick command to force old behavior for testing: `RUNTIME_KERNEL_HEUR=legacy ./bin/serve --test-profile`

mira: would a revert be acceptable? this is blocking the release canary.

elaine: I can cut a revert PR for the kernel-scoring tweak in ~20m. it will re-enable the width-based quantized path.

liam: bisect narrowed to range 0x9f300..0x9f3a2, suspecting the batching heuristic change that altered batch composition thresholds. bisect job: https://ci.internal/bisect/9876

sam: hold rollout on the canary, created PERF-4523 and linked CI + dashboard graphs. if revert proves safe we can re-run canary.

opsbot: @channel rollout paused for release/x canary by sam — reason: perf regression (PERF-4523).

mira: also noticed kernel-selector logs show increased entropy score for tiny sequences after that merge. snippet:
```
[02:14:58] kernel_selector: seq_len=16 score_entropy=0.73 score_latency=0.21 -> choose kernel 'fused_attention_v2'
[02:14:58] kernel_selector: quantized_path_available=false
```

liam: action plan: 1) finish bisect (me), 2) elaine cut revert if bisect confirms (elaine), 3) ops hold canary + unblock on revert verification (mira/tom), 4) add a defensive guard in selector to prefer quantized path when available for short sequences (follow-up).

elaine: opened revert PR https://git.internal/r/redwood/pull/3210 — CI running. PR description includes perf regression tests.

ci-bot: [perf-ci] revert PR #3210 queued for perf run. expected completion in ~12m.

tom: if revert doesn't land, short-term config toggle: set `kernel_selector.prefer_entropy=false` in prod-config to restore old dispatch. ops can flip it if needed.

sam: thanks. we'll reconvene after bisect + perf run completes. leaving notes on the dashboard and PERF-4523. :white_check_mark:

mira: adding a profiler job to nightly that snapshots kernel selection histograms so we can catch this earlier next time.

liam: bisect complete — root cause pinned to batching threshold change in commit 0x9f39f that reduced batch coalescing for short contexts. reverting that commit restores kv miss rate to ~0.05 and p95 back to baseline in smoke runs.

sam: great. closing loop once revert PR passes. thanks all. :pray:
